gates.evidence: The proposal targets 's07' (Create Account Sheet) and 's27' (Attachment and Mode Sheet), which are standard, brand-safe utility screens in Luzia.
The action is to 'Play a quick 15-second game' and the reward is '30 minutes of deep reasoning mode' with no cash-like elements, clicks, or installs.
The offer says 'Play a quick 15-second game to unlock 30 minutes of deep reasoning.' which uses positive gain framing without dark patterns or fake timers.
The proposal uses a standard opt-in button on s07 with 'Play Now' and 'No Thanks' as controls.
The body text states 'Play a quick 15-second game to unlock 30 minutes of deep reasoning.' which clearly discloses the action and length.
The offer card contains a visible 'No Thanks' option which closes the sheet and returns the user to s27 with no penalty.
The trigger occurs when trying to toggle deep reasoning on the attachment and mode sheet (s27), before any chat response begins.
The eligibility is limited to 'Non-paying guests and free users hitting the deep reasoning paywall.'

scores.evidence: Tapping 'Deep reasoning' on s27 block creates immediate intent. However, the patch grants '+1 Luzia+ Subscription' (resource r1) instead of a temporary pass. Rule 7 dictates that rewards treating an entitlement as a currency must score at most 2.

Bypassing the standard account wall s07 with a rewarded ad competes directly with the free sign-up flow, which stands in for a core action. This is highlighted by the code gate failing 'not-for-account-wall'.
The 30-minute time-box, non-payer eligibility, and daily cap of 2 limits substitution. However, granting r1 in the patch technically gives full plan access.
Cost to serve ($0.0090) exceeds the net revenue per view ($0.0063) at the low end. It is unprofitable for the premium model to run unlimited queries for 30 minutes under a single ad view.
Deep reasoning is a core capability and m9 has a 'frequent' reach on s07 as users try out the smarter modes.

Maps to SIM-RWD and uses a simple button entry. However, tracking time-boxed sessions inside a full subscription plan (r1) requires extra tracking infrastructure not standard for standard plan states.
Properly references screens s27, s07, and deep reasoning elements. It loses some credit due to treating r1 as a currency, failing rule limits on plan nouns.
Strong cap limits: 2 session passes per day maximum and a 30-minute cooldown.
Specifies a clear 10% user-level randomized holdout over 28 days with defined guardrails for conversion and retention.

requiredChanges: Modify the reward to be query-limited (e.g. '3 Deep Reasoning queries' instead of a 30-minute session pass) or implement a 2-view ad bundle to offset the $0.0090 premium model cost-to-serve.
Do not grant +1 Luzia+ Subscription (r1) in the patch. Update the patch to track and grant a custom temporary state rather than treating the subscription plan as a currency.
Relocate the reward invite so it does not compete directly on the sign-up wall. Only display the rewarded ad option after the user has explicitly declined the s07 Create Account sheet.
parsed.topConcern: The unit economics are highly unfavorable; the premium model's inference cost ($0.0090) exceeds the ad's net revenue at the low end. Additionally, granting a standard plan entitlement directly in the patch violates rule restrictions on currency behavior.
